title: The Absolute Effect - Master Trial Roster
rules: One entry represents one underlying trial/study, not one publication.
Trial aliases, acronyms, registry names and follow-up publications are collapsed into the same entry.
A trial-page entry counts as uploaded evidence.
A unique Trial-of-the-Day archived in data/trial-archive.json counts even if no permanent trial page exists.
Daily proposal files are not added merely because a trial was proposed; they must correspond to an uploaded trial page or archived Trial-of-the-Day to enter this roster.
Before future selection, this roster must be checked together with current Trial-of-the-Day and archive data.
After an approved daily batch is uploaded, the roster is updated the same day before subsequent daily selection.

Daily selection must avoid not only duplicate trials/studies but also consecutive trials that answer essentially the same clinical question; selection should maximize distinct clinical questions unless replication/evolution is deliberate.

Every trial page must remain visually informative when neither NNT nor NNH can be defensibly calculated: show a chart/pictogram of the strongest reported outcome (e.g. survival, response, progression, toxicity, or relative effect) using source-reported values only; label endpoint and time horizon; never derive NNT from median survival.

Every permanent trial page must distinguish historical trial results from current practice context. Audit for later follow-up publications, meta-analyses, guideline changes, and whether the intervention remains standard; display a dated current-practice context and linked sources. Do not overwrite original trial results with newer recommendations.

Do not mark a trial clinically current based only on its original publication date or presence of a source link. A freshness review must check subsequent follow-up, later practice-changing trials/meta-analyses, current disease-specific guideline recommendations, and whether the intervention remains standard; record dated sources and review status.

Every rostered and newly added trial page must be checked for an actual, readable outcome visualization: show a defensible NNT/NNH patient pictogram when possible; otherwise chart a source-reported survival, response, recurrence, toxicity, or relative-effect endpoint. Pages with no detectable numeric endpoint must be explicitly flagged for manual review rather than silently left as abstract-only. Never derive NNT from median survival.
Use a small shared set of treatment-setting categories across tumour sites; preserve the original specific setting in setting_detail and the full clinical question.

A batch is not releasable unless the latest-batch release validator passes: exact roster/page identity, canonical primary DOI link, no non-finite chart widths, no generic trial headings, no duplicated sections, and no conflicting NNT claims.

For every NNT/NNH pictogram, store the endpoint, time horizon, source-reported absolute percentage-point difference, and NNT/NNH in a structured absolute_effect object. data-benefit/data-harm must contain the absolute percentage-point differences, never 100 divided by NNT/NNH.
Do not calculate or display NNT from non-comparative trials, including randomized studies with an internal-control arm; display the source-reported outcome rates and state why NNT is not appropriate.

For randomized non-comparative designs with an internal control, show the arm-specific source-reported outcome rates as descriptive data; do not label the difference as absolute treatment benefit or render an NNT/NNH pictogram.

Any numeric NNT/NNH appearing anywhere on a trial page must be represented in absolute_effect with the exact endpoint and time horizon; pictogram values must equal the absolute percentage-point difference, not 100 divided by NNT/NNH.

Taxonomy: primary setting represents the treatment context, not disease extent. Relapsed / Refractory takes precedence when trial eligibility requires recurrence, progression on/after prior systemic therapy, or established treatment resistance. Advanced / Metastatic is reserved for advanced disease without a defining prior-progression/resistance requirement, including first-line treatment and maintenance in non-progressive disease.

Record disease extent, prior-treatment status, and treatment line as separate dimensions where supported by trial eligibility. A trial may be metastatic and relapsed/refractory simultaneously; do not duplicate the trial or force metastatic disease extent into the primary setting.

NSCLC-specific primary-setting taxonomy: use only Early, Metastatic, Adjuvant, Neoadjuvant, or Consolidation. Do not use Relapsed / Refractory, Advanced / Metastatic, Locally Advanced, Perioperative, or other primary-setting labels for NSCLC. Classify previously treated/progressed advanced NSCLC as Metastatic and retain relapse/progression/prior-line context in separate metadata or setting_detail. Use Neoadjuvant for perioperative trials whose treatment begins preoperatively; use Consolidation for post-definitive CRT systemic therapy; use Early for localized/locally advanced non-metastatic definitive-treatment trials.

trials.population: 563 patients without progression after initial platinum-etoposide plus durvalumab were randomized: tarlatamab-durvalumab n=282 and durvalumab n=281.

trials.setting_detail: Multimodality neoadjuvant treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer
trials.primary_title: Neoadjuvant Short-Course Radiotherapy Followed by Camrelizumab and Chemotherapy Versus Standard of Care for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (UNION): A Prespecified Interim Analysis of a Multicentre, Open-Label, Randomised, Phase 3 Trial
trials.population: 231 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer randomized between short-course RT followed by camrelizumab/CAPOX and standard long-course chemoradiotherapy-based care.
trials.intervention: Short-course radiotherapy 25 Gy in 5 fractions, followed by two cycles of camrelizumab 200 mg day 1 plus CAPOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1; capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14), then surgery and protocol adjuvant CAPOX plus camrelizumab.
trials.comparator: Long-course chemoradiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily on radiotherapy days, followed by surgery and protocol adjuvant CAPOX.
trials.primary_endpoint: Pathological complete response; event-free survival was a prespecified interim endpoint.
trials.follow_up: Prespecified interim analysis with three-year EFS; longer-term OS and late toxicity follow-up continue.
trials.efficacy: pCR 39.8% versus 15.3% (absolute difference 24.5 points; NNT 5). Three-year EFS 91.3% versus 77.4%; HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.15–0.71), P=0.0029, crossing the prespecified interim boundary. Absolute EFS difference 13.9 points; NNT 8.
trials.safety: Common grade 3–4 events included lymphopenia (20% versus 28%), neutropenia (12% versus 11%), diarrhoea (8% versus 3%) and nausea (8% versus 2%). One treatment-related death from radiation enteritis was reported in the control strategy.
trials.quality_of_life: No definitive QoL advantage was reported in the interim analysis.
trials.limitations: The experimental strategy changes RT fractionation, immunotherapy and systemic treatment together; the contribution of each component cannot be isolated. EFS is an interim analysis and should not be called mature OS.
trials.clinical_interpretation: UNION supports the studied short-course RT/camrelizumab/CAPOX strategy in locally advanced rectal cancer. The staged page's previous adjuvant schedule and overall grade ≥3 toxicity rates were not source-faithful and have been corrected.

trials.setting_detail: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after prior proteasome inhibitor and immunomodulatory therapy
trials.primary_title: Talquetamab–Daratumumab in Relapsed or Refractory Myeloma
trials.population: 864 patients with RRMM after at least one prior line including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor were randomized 1:1:1: Tal-DP n=287, Tal-D n=287, DPd n=290. Anti-CD38-refractory and prior GPRC5D-directed therapy were excluded.
trials.intervention: Talquetamab 0.8 mg/kg subcutaneously after step-up dosing plus daratumumab 1800 mg SC, with pomalidomide 4 mg orally days 1–21 and dexamethasone per protocol in the Tal-DP arm; Tal-D omitted pomalidomide.
trials.comparator: Daratumumab plus pomalidomide and dexamethasone (DPd).
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by independent review committee.
trials.follow_up: Interim analysis at median follow-up 24.6 months.
trials.efficacy: 24-month PFS 81.3% with Tal-DP, 77.6% with Tal-D and 51.2% with DPd; HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.20–0.40) and 0.33 (0.24–0.46), respectively; P<0.001 for both. ORR 88.2%, 88.5% and 77.6%; CR or better 71.1%, 69.0% and 34.5%; MRD-negative CR 52.3%, 46.3% and 15.9%. 24-month OS was 89.2%, 87.9% and 79.1%; OS superiority boundaries were not crossed.
trials.safety: Grade 3–4 AEs occurred in 96.7% with Tal-DP, 78.8% with Tal-D and 95.8% with DPd; grade 3–4 infections 37.7%, 29.2% and 42.4%. Serious AEs 63.0%, 52.6% and 53.7%; fatal AEs 1.8%, 4.0% and 4.6%. CRS, dysgeusia, weight loss, skin/nail effects, infection and cytopenias are important.
trials.quality_of_life: No definitive comparative QoL advantage was established in the primary abstract; characteristic GPRC5D-related oral/skin toxicity affects treatment burden.
trials.limitations: Three-arm interim analysis; OS is not yet statistically established. Prior anti-CD38 and GPRC5D exposure were restricted, so generalizability to refractory populations is limited.
trials.clinical_interpretation: Both Tal-DP and Tal-D significantly improve PFS versus DPd in the studied RRMM population. The previous staged page incorrectly used a two-arm comparison and wrong median PFS; this page restores the three-arm primary analysis.

trials.setting_detail: First-line maintenance strategy for advanced BRCA-non-mutated epithelial ovarian cancer
trials.primary_title: Chemotherapy With or Without Pembrolizumab Followed by Maintenance Pembrolizumab With or Without Olaparib as First-Line Treatment of Patients With Advanced BRCA Non-Mutated Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (ENGOT-OV43/GOG-3036/KEYLYNK-001): A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 3 Trial
trials.population: 1367 patients randomized 1:1:1: pembrolizumab-olaparib n=455, pembrolizumab n=458 and control n=454. All had stage III–IV BRCA1/2 non-mutated epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube cancer; prior PARP inhibitor or checkpoint inhibitor was excluded.
trials.intervention: All arms received five cycles of carboplatin plus paclitaxel (or docetaxel) with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks or matched placebo. Maintenance: pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w for up to 35 cycles plus olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily for up to 2 years, or matched placebo. Bevacizumab was permitted at investigator discretion.
trials.comparator: Two comparators: pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy followed by pembrolizumab/placebo maintenance; and placebo plus chemotherapy followed by placebo maintenance.
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS, tested hierarchically first in PD-L1 CPS ≥10 and then in the intention-to-treat population.
trials.follow_up: Final PFS analysis at median follow-up 49.6 months; OS data were not reported as a definitive mature benefit in this analysis.
trials.efficacy: At final analysis, pembrolizumab-olaparib improved PFS versus control: HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53–0.83) in CPS ≥10 and HR 0.71 (0.61–0.84) in ITT. At first interim analysis HRs were 0.63 and 0.68, respectively. Pembrolizumab alone was not significant in CPS ≥10 (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.77–1.19; P=0.33); therefore formal ITT testing for this arm was not performed.
trials.safety: Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 297/452 (66%) with pembrolizumab-olaparib, 255/456 (56%) with pembrolizumab and 232/454 (51%) with control. Serious treatment-related AEs were 24%, 21% and 9%; treatment-related deaths occurred in 4, 1 and 0 patients, respectively. Neutropenia and anaemia were common.
trials.quality_of_life: No definitive QoL superiority was established in the abstract; maintenance duration and hematologic burden are important.
trials.limitations: Three-arm hierarchical design; pembrolizumab alone did not improve PFS and cannot be interpreted as equivalent to the olaparib-containing arm. OS benefit is not established in this report.
trials.clinical_interpretation: The PFS signal is driven by pembrolizumab plus olaparib maintenance after chemotherapy, not pembrolizumab alone. The previous staged page's two-arm/median-PFS simplification was inadequate and is corrected.
